sources.entry: Paper: AutoGen: Enabling Next-Gen LLM Applications via Multi-Agent Conversation Framework

summary.name: AutoGen
summary.one_liner: AutoGen is an open-source Microsoft Research framework for building LLM applications in which multiple customizable agents converse with each other, with LLMs, humans, and tools as possible backends.
keywords: agents that write and run code
use_cases: dynamic group chat between AI agents
summary.what_it_does: AutoGen lets developers define agents that can send and receive messages, with each agent backed by LLMs, human input, tools, or a combination. Agents reply automatically to incoming messages through a unified send/receive/generate_reply interface, so conversations can run without a separate control module. Developers can control flow with natural language prompts, Python code, or custom reply functions. Built-in agents include ConversableAgent, AssistantAgent, and UserProxyAgent, plus a GroupChatManager for dynamic multi-agent group chats. The paper reports evaluations on math (MATH dataset), retrieval-augmented chat, and other example applications.
notable: Conversation programming paradigm mixing natural language and code to define agent workflows
Built-in AssistantAgent and UserProxyAgent that can execute LLM-suggested code or function calls
GroupChatManager for dynamic next-speaker selection in multi-agent chats
Arxiv paper 2308.08155 by Microsoft Research and collaborators
caveats: The page is the research paper; it does not describe current installation or licensing details beyond calling it open-source
Evaluation comparisons in the paper were limited by cost and message-rate constraints for some baselines
